summary: An official list of site idents for organizations on the ARPANET, given in alphabetical order and by network address. It covers sites with present or scheduled direct connections. Scheduled sites are marked with an s and inactive addresses with an i.

eli5.summary: A list of short nicknames for each organization on the network and the number of its door, so everybody uses the same names.

questions: list of arpanet site names and addresses
what do s and i mean in the site list
subtitle: The August 1972 official list of site names and address numbers for organizations on the ARPA Network.

tldr.problem: People on the ARPA Network needed one agreed short name and address number for each connected organization.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC prints two lists of idents, one in alphabetical order and one by site address, with marks for scheduled and inactive sites.
tldr.outcome: It replaces RFC 289 as the official list as of 28 August 1972.

today: RFC 384 obsoletes RFC 289. It lists the network as it stood in August 1972 and should not be read as a current directory.

sections.title: Official Idents
sections.content:
Jeanne B. North of the ARPA Network Information Center published this list on 28 August 1972. It obsoletes RFC 289.

It includes only organizations with present or scheduled direct connection to the Network. Scheduled sites are marked s and inactive addresses are marked i.
sections.eli5: This is the official name list for the network, and it only includes places that are connected or about to be.

sections.title: Reading the Alphabetical List
sections.content:
The first list has three columns: Site Ident, Address and Organization. Examples are UCLA-NMC at address 1 (Network Measurement Center), SRI-ARC at 2 and UTAH-10 at 4.

Some entries simply say see another ident, such as AMEC see Belvoir. A dash in place of an address, as for AFETR and LLL, means no address is given yet; both are scheduled.
sections.eli5: Each place has a short nickname and a number. Some nicknames just point you to the real one, like a sign saying see the other door.

sections.title: The List by Address
sections.content:
The second list gives the same sites in number order, starting with the entries that have no address and then address 1 upward. Besides the main host entries, it shows TIP sites with higher numbers, such as ARPA-TIP at 156 and MIT-ML at 198.

A few numbers are shared. ICCC and FNWC both appear at 161, both marked as scheduled.
sections.eli5: The second list puts the same places in number order, like houses on a street, so you can look up who lives at a number.
